title: Locale formatting and translation roundtrip prompt bank (CJK and RTL)
content:
Purpose:
This prompt bank and companion notes are a working collection for onboarding new model variants to Redwood’s hosted and dedicated runtimes with a focus on:
- CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) handling (punctuation width, tokenizer segmentation, numerals)
- RTL scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and bidi interactions
- Translation quality checks (adequacy + fluency) for en<->xx pairs
- Locale-sensitive formatting (dates, times, currency, units, address formats)

Scope and usage notes:
- Intended for use by applied-ml engineers and annotators during model onboarding and regression testing.
- Prompts are organized to be short, synthetic, and also longer-context scenarios to exercise tokenization, KV cache behaviour, and streaming output.
- Mix of machine-checkable golden answers and manual annotation targets.

Evaluation categories and rubrics (short):
1) Translation adequacy: preserves meaning and core entities (score 0-3).
2) Fluency/naturalness: idiomatic target language style (0-3).
3) Locale formatting correctness: dates, numbers, currency, phone/address formatting (pass/fail + comment).
4) Script integrity: no stray LTR/RTL markers, proper punctuation orientation (pass/fail).
5) Preservation of domain tokens: product names, acronyms, code snippets (pass/fail).

Automation checks (examples):
- Unicode category checks: ensure numerals converted to expected script (e.g., Arabic-Indic digits vs Western digits) when locale implies it.
- Bidi sanitizer: no unmatched directional override characters (RLO/LRO), and strong directionality matches expected language.
- Date normalization: parse and re-format dates according to target locale (YYYY-?? -> expected).
- Roundtrip BLEU/chrF for automated signals (supplementary, not sole metric).

Prompt bank (examples). Keep each prompt labeled with language/tag and test intent. These are intentionally terse for easy batching in eval harness.

-- CJK: tokenization / punctuation / full-width vs half-width --
1) zh-simplified-tokenization-1: "把 2024/12/31 的發票號碼：INV-00987 寄給王先生。"
   intent: punctuation/number normalization; expected: keeps invoice ID intact; date formatted per zh-CN conventions (2024年12月31日) for locale output tasks.

2) zh-traditional-space-handling: "請把報表存成CSV，儲存在D:\資料\月報.csv。"
   intent: filesystem path with backslashes + CJK; check escaping and bytewise preservation.

3) ja-wide-halfwidth-mix: "請把顯示器設定為 27" Full HD（1920×1080）並儲存。"
   intent: mixed width quotes/units; expect correct handling of double-quote inches symbol and full-width parentheses.

4) ko-number-grouping: "총 금액은 1,200,000원입니다. 영수증 번호: R-77."
   intent: currency symbol placement and digit grouping; ensure no tokenization splits digits incorrectly.

-- RTL: bidi, vowels, and address formatting --
5) ar-simple-address: "أرسل الفاتورة إلى مكتب الرياض، شارع الملك فهد ٥٤٢。"
   intent: Arabic address normalization and ordinal/number glyphs (use Arabic-Indic digits if locale expects).

6) he-bidi-mix: "שלום, הכנסת הערך 3/4 בדוח — האם זה נכון?"
   intent: mixed punctuation and fractions in Hebrew; check visual order in rendered output.

-- Translation roundtrip short forms --
7) en->zh->en-roundtrip: source: "Please schedule a meeting with the Tokyo engineering team next Thursday at 3pm JST."
   pipeline: model translates to zh, then retranslate to en (same model or paired variant).
   expectation: meeting time, timezone (JST), and weekday preserved; minor phrasing changes allowed.

8) en->ar->en-technical-term-preserve: source: "Upgrade the Redis cache to v7.0 and test persistence under 1M writes."
   check: technical tokens preserved; numbers unchanged; meaning preserved.

-- Locale formatting stress tests --
9) date-ambiguity-en: "02/03/2026" with locale zh-CN vs en-US; prompt: "Format the date above for local display (zh-CN)."
   expectation: "2026年3月2日" (if day-month reversed).

10) currency-unit-switch: "Convert $1,250.75 to the local display for ko-KR and ar-SA (assume no conversion rate change)."
    check: currency symbol placement and decimals.

Manual annotation instructions (short):
- For roundtrip tasks, annotators mark: (A) core-meaning-preserved (Y/N), (B) important entities preserved (list), (C) notable hallucinations (free text).
- For locale-formatting tasks, annotators add a short normalized example and mark pass/fail on each element (date, number grouping, currency, phone).
- For bidi tasks, annotators view rendering in a bidi-aware viewer (we provide preview tool link in linked_artifacts) and mark visual anomalies.

Known tricky cases / guidelines:
- Mixed LTR tokens inside RTL text: keep ASCII tokens intact but be careful with surrounding spaces; model sometimes inserts invisible directionality controls.
- Han variants: Mainland vs Taiwan variant preferences are data-driven; for onboarding we default to the model's configured locale unless explicitly testing variant conversion.
- Tokenizer clipping: long CJK continuous strings (e.g., concatenated hashtags) can cause high token counts — add a stress prompt to exercise batching.

Stress prompt (long context):
- cn-long-chat-log: 1200-character Chinese customer chat concatenated from support logs (synthetic) asking to summarize action items, preserve dates and numbers. Purpose: exercise KV cache and ensure summarization preserves numeric entities.

Quick checklist for an onboarding run:
1) Run automated Unicode + bidi checks over generated outputs.
2) Run translation roundtrip pipeline; compute chrF and a small set of semantic similarity signals.
3) Sample 200 outputs for manual annotation across categories (CJK/RTL/locale-formatting/roundtrip).
4) Collate failures into JIRA tickets with reproducible prompts, model config, and deterministic seed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Create a small set of audio/TTS prompts to check numeral pronunciation in different locales (linked to CONF-4456).
- Add test cases for vertical Japanese text rendering (product docs edge-case).
- Decide on a single canonical rule for Arabic-Indic vs Western digits per customer locale mapping.

References and quick links (internal):
- Eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-evals (see docs/locale-tests)
- Confluence spec: CONF-4456: Locale-formatting-eval-playbook
- Related tickets: JIRA-ML-2019, JIRA-I18N-802

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working prompt bank: please flag prompts that are ambiguous or language-inappropriate.
- If you add examples, keep filename-friendly labels and add the test intent line.

-- end of document --
